field.p: (Originally posted by NH7X on January 29, 2015)

Dear Fellow Contester: since you enjoy participating in shorter domestic SSB contests, we want to be sure you're aware of an exciting four hour event of this type coming up this Saturday, January 31st - the North American SSB Sprint! The NA SSB Sprint runs on 20m, 40m and 80m this Saturday afternoon/evening:

Time zones:
UTC: 00z-04z
AST: 8pm-12am
EST: 7pm-11pm
CST: 6pm-10pm
MST: 5pm-9pm
PST: 4pm-8pm
AKST: 3pm-7pm
HST: 2pm-6pm

ul.li: Four-hour duration, ideal for participants with limited availability
Categories for QRP, Low Power (100w), and High Power with separate awards
Individual entry or team registration (up to 5 members)
Unique QSY rule requiring a 5kHz minimum frequency change after CQ
Multiple award opportunities including t-shirts, plaques, certificates, and achievement recognition
Random drawing for door prizes from all submitted logs

field.p: ssbsprint.com has the contest rules, a multiplier checklist, logging software guidance, operating tips, and planned activity tracking.
73 and CU in the Sprint! NA SSB Sprint Committee, Contest Manager: Chris Tate, N6WM

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by W1EJ on September 22, 2016)

Continuing my quest to reach 100 Activator points and 500 Chaser points by the end of the year. This week's trip took me to the Burney, CA area, with a plan to activate three summits: Soldier Mountain, Burney Mountain, and Lassen Peak. Got to Soldier Mountain's summit late afternoon, but 20 meters was still open for most of my contacts. Gorgeous view of the Fall River Valley to the east - almost like looking at Google Earth - plus Shasta to the north and Lassen to the southwest.

Next morning I went up Burney Mountain. The last few miles of road are not for the faint of heart - lucky I met no one coming the other way. Wind at the top was roaring, so I started with my MFJ 20m loaded whip. After about six contacts on 20 CW I wanted to try other bands, so I put up my 20 ft pole with 39 feet of wire. Worked more on 20 and several on 40, though the wind was bending the pole way over. The fire tower is staffed, so there's access to a pit toilet! Headed to Lassen Park after that looking for a campsite, but after checking the weather (high winds, cold, showers) decided to save Lassen for next summer.
If you like the outdoors, SOTA is great fun. Anyone want to join me on the next outing?

Mike, W6STR

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by W1EJ on October 10, 2016)

Thanks Mike. The last two summits that got me over 100 were a bit of a challenge - North Yolla Bolly and Black Rock Mountain, in the Shasta Trinity National Forest about sixty miles west of Red Bluff. Did both in one day since they're only about four miles apart. Camped at the trailhead and got an early start. The hike up to Pettijohn Basin between them is along a nice but sometimes steep trail. Did North Yolla Bolly in the morning, then Black Rock - the trail gets indistinct and pretty steep the last half mile. Glad I had the Garmin! A lot of work for one day, but the views from the summits were fabulous and HF propagation even better. Next year I'm planning to backpack and camp in the basin between them. By the way, I see you're #10 on the W6 Chasers list - wow!

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by N6DMR on October 10, 2017)

An enthusiastic endorsement of Digital Mobile Radio (DMR) - good evening QSOs with Phil K6AXY across the country. Both using Radioddity GD-77 dual-band DMR radios and SharkRF OpenSPOT repeaters. My OpenSPOT connects via an AT&T mobile hotspot in the motorhome, which has made for several QSOs on Talk Group 3100 North America. N6DMR seems to be catching on in the DMR community.

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by N6DMR on October 12, 2017)

"Adhoc Talk Groups" let you set up private or group DMR communications - you pick a custom talk group number, and once you key up on it, anyone else keying that same number joins in. Tested this with a temporary TG number (31000077) and confirmed it works for both a private two-way contact and a semi-private multi-user group, just by sharing the TG number.

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by N6DMR on October 17, 2017)

Recommend Contact Manager, a third-party code plug editor that supports Motorola and TYT radios. Its documentation includes useful tips for avoiding common configuration mistakes - a solid resource for anyone programming a DMR radio.

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted anonymously for K6YA on June 23, 2025)
K6YA is inviting contacts via AX.25 packet on Field Day - monitoring 145.050 MHz Saturday from 1100 to 1700 Pacific time, from grid square CM87xh.
Suggested exchange: "From: K6YA, To: CQ, CQ Field Day K6YA," followed by your call sign, station class, and section - K6YA will respond "K6YA 3A SCV." Digital QSO contacts count two points each.

K6YA can reach digipeaters KBERR, KBETH, KJOHN, and WOODY, and also accepts messages at K6YA@winlink.org in standard NTS or ICS-213 format - per the Field Day 2025 rules, messages that "leave or enter the Field Day operation via amateur radio RF" can earn 10 bonus points each, up to 100 points total.
